title: ECR Image Scan Findings

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay sample `aws:ecr:scan` events with `severity="CRITICAL" OR severity="HIGH"` into `index=aws`. Confirm UC-4.1.52 returns >=1 row and the alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `aws:ecr:scan` traffic without `severity="CRITICAL" OR severity="HIGH"`. Confirm UC-4.1.52 returns zero rows and the alert does not fire.

dataSources: `index=aws` sourcetype=`aws:ecr:scan` collected via `Splunk_TA_aws`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=aws sourcetype="aws:ecr:scan" severity="CRITICAL" OR severity="HIGH"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.52_ecr_image_scan_findings_52"
| sort -_time
description: UC-4.1.52 — ECR Image Scan Findings: queries AWS `aws:ecr:scan` for search criteria `severity="CRITICAL" OR severity="HIGH"` and returns actor, resource, and region context for security review and change validation.
value: On AWS, detecting 'ECR Image Scan Findings' early shortens cloud incident response and produces defensible audit evidence for identity and change-management controls. UC-4.1.52 drives high-priority security alerting before customer-impacting drift.
implementation: Enable ECR image scanning (enhanced or basic). Send scan completion events to EventBridge; forward to Splunk. Alert on CRITICAL/HIGH in repos tagged as production. Block deployment in pipeline when findings exceed threshold.
visualization: Table (repo, tag, severity, CVE), Bar chart (findings by repo), Trend line (findings over time).
cimSpl:
| tstats `summariesonly` count
  from datamodel=Intrusion_Detection.IDS_Attacks
  where match(lower(IDS_Attacks.severity), "high|critical")
  by IDS_Attacks.signature IDS_Attacks.src span=1d

detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=aws`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_aws` with the modular input for `aws:ecr:scan`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.1.78.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Enable ECR image scanning (enhanced or basic). Send scan completion events to EventBridge; forward to Splunk. Alert on CRITICAL/HIGH in repos tagged as production. Block deployment in pipeline when findings exceed threshold.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:ecr:scan" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:ecr:scan" severity="CRITICAL" OR severity="HIGH"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.52_ecr_image_scan_findings_52"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:ecr:scan` in `index=aws` to detect ecr image scan findings. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_1_52_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Table (repo, tag, severity, CVE), Bar chart (findings by repo), Trend line (findings over time)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_aws` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of ecr image scan findings so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
